title: John J. Appleton → John Quincy Adams, Cadiz, despatch with an 18-group coded passage on the Spanish liberal government's secret English loan, printed 'no decodification'
correspondents: John James Appleton (US chargé d'affaires ad interim at Madrid, with the Cortes at Cadiz) → John Quincy Adams, Secretary of State
shelfmark: NARA RG 59, Despatches from US Ministers to Spain, vol. 22 (20 May 1822-30 Dec 1823) = microfilm M31 reel 24, catalog naId 188609418
folio_note: 18 code groups in the body (Manning prints them: 1088 648 1576 794 1384 1453 347 1372 500 192 668 1384 169 1244 1501 1110 1426 1290; several OCR-uncertain); frame not located
status: Manning, Diplomatic Correspondence ... Independence of the Latin-American Nations (1925) vol. 3, doc. 1124, p. 2041, prints the groups with '[no decodification]'. The groups fit the code rebuilt in targets/jqa (the = 1385, of = 1576, that = 1384, and = 668; the London/St Petersburg code): with targets/jqa/code_table.tsv 16 of 18 groups take a value ('... of [794] that ... was [192] and that he had a part in England'). Not in the repo (known.py: Appleton no hits).
why: The Spanish constitutional government's secret plan to raise money in England in the last weeks of the Cortes at Cadiz (1823), told to the US chargé by the finance minister Yandiola; directly readable with a key this repository already holds.
score_note: Scored from the printed edition (Manning 1925) during the Oct 2026 NARA/State Department sweep (research/nara_state/); not viewed
verify: Find the despatch on M31 reel 24 (naId 188609418, 329 frames), re-transcribe the 18 groups and decode with targets/jqa/code_table.tsv; check the other Appleton despatches of 1822-23 in the same volume for more code.

title: Alexander H. Everett → Henry Clay, Madrid, despatch on his audience about Spanish America with six lines in cipher 'without decodification'
correspondents: Alexander Hill Everett (US minister to Spain) → Henry Clay, Secretary of State
shelfmark: NARA RG 59, Despatches from US Ministers to Spain, vol. 25 (17 Mar 1825-18 Apr 1826) = microfilm M31 reel 27, catalog naId 188610348
folio_note: six lines of cipher in the body, after the minister's (Zea Bermúdez's) declaration that the King would never abandon his claim to the colonies
status: Manning 1925 vol. 3, doc. 1134, p. 2002: '[Here follow six lines in cipher, without decodification.]'. Everett's code not identified; the Legation in Madrid also held the code used by Appleton in 1823 (the targets/jqa family), the first thing to test. Not in the repo (known.py: Everett no hits).
why: Everett's confidential report of Spain's position on recognising the new American states after Ayacucho; the six lines are the part he hid.

title: Joel Roberts Poinsett → James Monroe, Santiago de Chile, despatch with at least nine cipher passages printed as '(undeciphered cipher)'
correspondents: Joel Roberts Poinsett (US special agent and consul general for Buenos Aires, Chile and Peru) → James Monroe, Secretary of State
shelfmark: NARA RG 59, Despatches from Special Agents, vol. 3 (Poinsett 1813-23) = microfilm M37 roll 2, catalog naId 213803757; Poinsett's other 1811-14 reports ('parts in cipher') are in the Poinsett Papers vol. 4, Historical Society of Pennsylvania (Gilpin collection)
folio_note: nine '(undeciphered cipher)' insertions in Manning's text, single words to whole clauses (on the Carreras, the Buenos Aires army, the Portuguese, the Araucanian chief); frame of the letter not located (M37 roll 2 frames 16-24 are the Poinsett list and his 'State of society' essay)
status: Manning 1925 vol. 2, doc. 442, pp. 896-897, prints the despatch with '(undeciphered cipher)' at each coded passage; the State Department returned Poinsett's other letters to him in 1818, so his own copies (some 'Part in cipher', May-July 1811 from Buenos Aires, per the HSP list filmed at M37 roll 2 frames 20-22) are at HSP, possibly with plaintext drafts. Not in the repo (known.py: Poinsett no hits).
why: Poinsett was an active partisan of the Carreras in the first Chilean republic; the hidden passages are his own views on the Chilean leadership and the war with Peru, otherwise unrecorded in US files.
score_note: Scored from the printed edition (Manning 1925) and the M37 roll 2 finding list (frames 0016-0024 viewed) during the Oct 2026 NARA/State Department sweep (research/nara_state/); the letter itself not viewed
verify: Locate the 20 Feb 1813 letter on M37 roll 2 (after frame 0024); identify the cipher (the cypher sent with his 1810 instructions); check the HSP Poinsett Papers vol. 4 for drafts and the other ciphered reports of 1811.

title: Joel Roberts Poinsett → Secretary of State, Buenos Aires reports 'part(s) in cipher' (Elío's mediation, defeat in Upper Peru, Brazil), returned to Poinsett in 1818
correspondents: Joel Roberts Poinsett → Robert Smith / James Monroe, Secretary of State
shelfmark: Historical Society of Pennsylvania, Poinsett Papers (Gilpin collection), vol. 4 (list of his official reports 1811-1815, filmed in NARA M37 roll 2 frames 0020-0022)
folio_note: three reports marked 'Part in cipher' / 'Parts in cipher' in the HSP list; extent unknown
status: The typed list of Poinsett's official reports in the HSP collection (filmed by NARA at the head of M37 vol. 3) marks these three as partly in cipher; Manning 1925 says the Department's copies were sent back to Poinsett in 1818 and are not in RG 59. Whether they were ever deciphered is not stated.
why: The earliest US agent's reports from revolutionary Buenos Aires; the ciphered parts concern British mediation and the Portuguese-Brazilian threat.

date: 1822 (duplicate intercepted in France; delivered at Bogotá, transmitted 19 Jan 1824)
title: José Rafael Revenga → Colombian Secretary of Foreign Affairs, Madrid, letter partly in cipher intercepted by the French, sent to Washington by Anderson with no key
correspondents: José Rafael Revenga (Colombian envoy in Spain) → Pedro Gual, Secretary of Foreign Affairs of Colombia (paper enclosed by Richard C. Anderson, US minister at Bogotá → John Quincy Adams)
shelfmark: NARA RG 59, Despatches from US Ministers to Colombia, vol. 3, enclosure 'No. 4' (paper in fragments) to Anderson's despatch of 19 Jan 1824 (microfilm T33)
folio_note: a paper in fragments, written partly in cipher; Manning: 'Not printed. A postscript to Anderson's letter explains that no key to the cipher was furnished. The portions not in cipher are, alone, unintelligible.'
status: Manning 1925 vol. 2, doc. 641, pp. 1272-73. Gual told Anderson it was the duplicate of a Revenga letter from Madrid sent through France, intercepted and opened there, then handed by Count Landos (a French agent at Cartagena, 1822) to a Colombian agent. Revenga's other cipher letters (Archivo General de la Nación, Bogotá; Archivo Santander) may share the key. Not in the repo (known.py: Revenga no hits).
why: Colombia's first envoy to Spain reporting on the 1822 negotiations for recognition, a letter the French secret service read and the Colombians passed to the US to warn of French designs.
score_note: Scored from the printed edition (Manning 1925) during the Oct 2026 NARA/State Department sweep (research/nara_state/); not viewed
